stem:
Sahil folds a sheet so each fold doubles the current thickness. The starting thickness is 0.1 mm. He wants the thickness after k folds.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: Add 2 mm at each fold to the starting thickness.
Multiply the starting thickness by k only, ignoring that each fold acts on the current thickness.
Replace "double" with "add two" and sum 0.1 + 2 + 2 + … for k folds.
Start at 0.1 mm and multiply by 2 at each fold (repeated multiplication).

teacher.key_rationale: Doubling each time is repeated multiplication by 2 on the current thickness. Adding 2 mm reverses multiplication into addition; multiplying only by k omits the successive-current condition; reading "double" as "add two" substitutes the wrong operation word.

mx_swap.reason: Excluded-case prose about when to use repeated multiplication is author talk; kept relationship_reversal, condition_omission, term_substitution on the doubling hinge.
